Samsung is in talks to acquire Modine Manufacturing, a US-listed maker of cooling systems for data centres, Bloomberg News reported on Thursday (Nov 12), citing people familiar with the matter.  The companies are discussing a potential deal that could come together as soon as the coming weeks, the report added. Shares of Modine surged 29 per cent in extended trading following the report. The company had a market value of US$5.6 billion as of Thursday, according to data compiled by LSEG. No final decision has been made and the talks could still fall apart, the report said, adding that another suitor could also emerge. Reuters could not immediately verify the report. Samsung and Modine could not be reached for comment immediately.

Source: Reuters/nh

WASHINGTON: United States House Speaker Mike Johnson said on Thursday (Nov 12) there was growing consensus in Congress on limiting chip exports to China after a spy scandal forced out Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang . Huang stepped down after reports of a romantic relationship with a businesswoman whom US authorities suspect of spying for the Chinese government.  Lawmakers from both parties have since called for tougher restrictions on China's access to advanced artificial intelligence chips, threatening access to chips that underpin China's surging AI development. Nvidia's advanced AI chips are widely used to develop cutting-edge AI models, making the company key to the US race against China to build superior AI systems. The US has sought for years to limit China’s access to Nvidia’s chips because it does not want the Chinese military to benefit from them.

"The export controls on chips to China has been a big issue around here," Johnson, a Louisiana Republican, told reporters at the US Capitol, adding he favoured limiting China's access to the advanced technology.  "I think there's a developing consensus in Congress that is an important position to take." The Chinese businesswoman, Alice Huang, was an executive at Megaspeed , an Nvidia partner the US government suspects of helping China obtain advanced AI chips restricted under US export controls. Beijing has denied Alice Huang is a spy.

Related:

Who is Alice Huang, Chinese exec accused of spying on Nvidia CEO?

Commentary: Everything Jensen Huang said about China is out the window

REPUBLICANS EYE EXPORT RESTRICTIONS The case has revived claims among China critics in Washington that US export policies are too weak, boosting calls for more restrictions. Reuters reported that Chinese AI companies are trying to rent Nvidia-powered computing capacity outside China because they are worried the Jensen Huang allegations could spur Washington to tighten restrictions on their ability to access the company's chips remotely.   Congressional Republicans are keen to attach new restrictions on exporting advanced AI chips to China in the annual defence authorisation Bill, a must-pass measure that funds the military and typically attracts bipartisan support, according to a Senate aide, who spoke on the condition of anonymity.  Lawmakers are pressing their colleagues to pass at least four Bills on chip exports, according to statements since Monday.  The AI Overwatch Act would give Congress more power over advanced AI chip exports. The Chip Security Act would require companies to track the location of advanced AI processors to prevent smuggling.  The Match Act would pressure US allies to restrict sales and maintenance of advanced chipmaking equipment destined for China. The Remote Access Security Act would give the Commerce Department the tools to stop Chinese firms from renting overseas data centres to access Nvidia chips. Jensen Huang is separately expected to testify before Congress before Thanksgiving, which falls on Nov 26.  House Foreign Affairs Chairman Brian Mast, a Florida Republican, told reporters on Thursday that congressional staff spoke with Nvidia on Wednesday night about a date and location for his testimony.  Mast and two other leading House Republicans asked Huang last week to brief them behind closed doors about his relationship with the suspected Chinese spy.

Nov 12 : The US Treasury bought Japanese yen in the July-to-September quarter, but the Federal Reserve did not intervene on its own in foreign exchange markets in the same period, the Federal Reserve Bank of New York said on Thursday. The New York Fed's quarterly report on currency market operations detailed interventions executed on behalf of the Treasury this summer to stem a sharp weakening of the yen. The purchase was the first US yen-buying intervention since 1998, and the report shows Washington acted alongside Tokyo to support the Japanese currency. On July 30, press reports emerged that the New York Fed had requested "rate checks" on the dollar-yen rate. The New York Fed report said the checks were made "solely on behalf of the US Treasury," with the New York Fed acting as the government's fiscal agent. The yen rose 2.3 per cent against the dollar that day.

A Reuters photograph taken during a cabinet meeting at Camp David on July 31 showed a "to-do" list in which Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent appeared to be weighing US purchases of $5 billion to $10 billion worth of Japanese yen. The New York Fed said it bought 79.4 billion yen ($497.37 million) in the spot market on July 31, selling euros from the Exchange Stabilization Fund. The New York Fed made the purchase "to counter what the US Treasury viewed as disorderly moves in the Japanese yen," its report said. Japan's Ministry of Finance acted in coordination, intervening "in the amount of 15.4 trillion yen" during the quarter to counter what it saw as excessive volatility and disorderly yen moves, the New York Fed added. Bessent said on August 2 that the US "will not hesitate to participate in further joint intervention," while repeating calls for further interest rate hikes by the Bank of Japan. The yen recovered quickly. Between July 30 and August 3, the dollar-yen rate fell "from around 164 yen per dollar to around 155 yen per dollar," the report said. The yen has since weakened. Japan's top currency diplomat, Atsushi Mimura, warned on Thursday that it was "too early to forget" this summer's intervention as the yen moved back toward 160 per dollar, its weakest level since September. Analysts at Mizuho Securities flagged the risk of Japanese intervention, saying the dollar was likely to keep rising against the yen, supported by resilience in the US economy and persistently high inflation driven by strong AI investment. Some Bank of Japan policymakers called in October for speeding up rate hikes, arguing that underlying inflation has reached the central bank's 2 per cent target. Their remarks strengthen the case for near-term tightening. A majority of economists in a Reuters poll expect the BOJ to raise its policy rate to 1.5 per cent in December, extending the faster pace after increases in June and September. ($1 = 159.6400 yen)

Source: Reuters

Nov 12 : Anthropic's initial public offering has drawn about six times the orders for the shares available for what could be the largest first-time share sale, Bloomberg News reported on Thursday. Bankers told prospective investors that Anthropic will prioritize its existing backers, leaving some would-be buyers with smaller allocations than expected, the report added, citing people familiar with the matter. Details of the IPO, including the demand for shares, could change, according to the report. Anthropic could not immediately be reached for comment on the report. Anthropic's initial public offering will value the Claude chatbot creator at up to $1.4 trillion, slightly below some investor expectations, setting up a key test of Wall Street's confidence in the artificial intelligence boom. The AI lab and some of its existing shareholders are aiming to raise up to $64.4 billion in the IPO by selling 825 million shares priced between $70 and $78 each. Shares are expected to start trading on the Nasdaq on November 19 under the symbol "ANT."

Source: Reuters

SAO PAULO, Nov 12 : Brazilian digital lender Nubank posted third-quarter profit in line with analysts' estimates on Thursday, while improving its efficiency ratio projections for the year partly due to an artificial intelligence-led slowdown in hiring. Nubank parent Nu Holdings, which has over 140 million clients and in September began expanding beyond Latin America, now expects its full-year efficiency ratio, which measures how much a bank has to spend to generate revenue, to land between 19 per cent and 19.5 per cent, below a previous expectation of around 20 per cent. "The biggest thing is that our pace of hiring was a little bit slower than we expected," Chief Financial Officer Rob Livingston told Reuters. "We are seeing significant benefits from AI helping us with our capacity and productivity, and so we slowed down our hiring."  Livingston said Nubank's return-to-office policy, announced last year, was also rolling out more slowly than initially planned as the company is opening new offices in several cities, while stronger-than-expected revenue also boosted efficiency prospects.

PROFIT MATCHES ESTIMATES, SHARES UP Nubank reported $1.09 billion in net income for the July-September quarter, up 31 per cent from a year earlier on a currency-neutral basis and matching the Visible Alpha consensus. Revenue also came in roughly in line with market expectations at $6.26 billion, a 37 per cent boost.  Shares of the company were up around 4 per cent in extended trading following the results, after rising 2 per cent during the earnings conference call.  Nubank's credit portfolio grew by 33 per cent, while the 90-day delinquency ratio rose to 7.3 per cent from 6.7 per cent, a climb Livingston  attributed mostly to seasonal effects and an increase in risk between late last year and early this year. "We're not seeing any evidence of broad-based exogenous worsening in our portfolio," he said. "The increase is entirely due to management decisions and timing that we were anticipating," he noted. HIGH BAR ON ACQUISITIONS Nubank Chief Executive David Velez said in a call with analysts that the bank will look at potential mergers or acquisitions as it expands globally, but that it has a "strong preference" for organic growth. "The bar would have to be extremely high for us to do a full M&A," Velez said. The remarks came after media reports in September that Nubank was in talks to buy British digital bank Monzo in a £10 billion ($13.23 billion) deal, which sent Nubank shares lower at the time as investors pointed to the transaction's execution risk. Nubank said a few days later that it was not pursuing such a transaction. ($1 = 0.7556 pound)

Source: Reuters

Nov 12 : Kalshi is in talks to raise fresh funds at a $65 billion valuation to build a new platform for trading compute futures, a source familiar with the matter told Reuters on Thursday, days after announcing the finalization of its previous round. Kalshi could not immediately be reached for comment. The company raised $1 billion in a new funding round late last month amid efforts to expand beyond event contracts and compete more directly with traditional exchanges. The round was co-led by Sequoia and Wellington. The October fundraise came just over five months after Kalshi raised $1 billion in a Coatue-led round that valued the company at $22 billion.

RACE FOR COMPUTE FUTURES The move into compute futures would also be a part of the broader strategy of the prediction market startup in its venture into newer products, as it challenges the likes of CME Group and New York Stock Exchange parent Intercontinental Exchange. Compute futures are financial contracts allowing traders to hedge or speculate on the future prices of computing resources like cloud and GPU capacity. The derivatives help companies manage price volatility, lock in future processing power and cut costs in a fast-growing technology market. CME Group said earlier in the year that it was partnering with Silicon Data to launch compute futures later this year, pending regulatory review. ICE and Kalshi were also in the running for such products as Wall Street's push deepens for a derivative market for compute. "America cannot win the AI race without a robust derivatives market for compute," Commodity Futures Trading Commission Chairman Michael Selig said in a statement earlier in the year while calling for industry comments on such products. However, reports earlier in the week said that the regulator has postponed the approval of futures contracts tied to the rental price of graphics processing units as it plans to consult benchmark providers on price manipulation concerns in this nascent asset class.

Nov 12 : Cisco beat Wall Street estimates for first-quarter results and raised its annual revenue forecast on Thursday, as the network-gear maker bets on sustained strong demand from companies building out their AI infrastructure. The company has doubled down on its AI efforts through strategic investments as Big Tech's massive spending moves beyond AI processors to the switches and routers required to connect large data-center systems. Cisco expects fiscal 2027 revenue in the range of $74.8 billion to $75.8 billion, compared with its previous forecast of $72.2 billion to $73.4 billion. "We are in the very early stages of a multi-year networking supercycle," CEO Chuck Robbins said in a statement.

The company reported an adjusted profit of $1.40 per share for the quarter ended October 24, above estimates of $1.33. Cisco is also building software tools that businesses can use to build their own armies of bots, known as AI agents, to protect their IT infrastructure against cybersecurity threats. Shares of the San Jose, California-based company were flat in volatile extended trading. They have risen about 32 per cent so far this year through Thursday's close. Cisco's gross margin has been a worry for investors, as a shortage of memory chips has pushed up component costs for hardware makers while suppliers prioritize chips for AI data-center customers. "A small dip in gross margin is not a major concern given higher memory and component costs," said Bob O'Donnell, president and chief analyst at TECHnalysis Research. Cisco's raised annual forecast and results above estimates are what the market wants to see from a company tied to AI infrastructure, he added. The company reported first-quarter adjusted gross margin of 65.6 per cent, in line with estimates, but down from 68.1 per cent a year earlier.

Nov 12 : Cerebras Systems raised its 2026 revenue forecast and signed Microsoft as a customer, easing investor concerns about AI spending and sending the chip and cloud company's shares more than 17 per cent higher in extended trading on Thursday. The forecast signaled enduring demand for AI computing despite concerns driven by US voter opposition to data centers and uncertainty from Jensen Huang's exit from Nvidia. The stock had fallen 47.2 per cent from its May IPO price as investors grew wary of the massive infrastructure spending required to support AI growth. "As we look to the months ahead, we see two certainties: rapid change and compute shortages," Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman said on a call with analysts. He said Cerebras' job is to make sure it grows no matter how AI develops, whether customers want hardware or cloud capacity.

Cerebras is racing to support a deal to provide computing power for OpenAI, which underpins Cerebras' remaining performance obligations of $26.1 billion as of September 30. Feldman also said the company has signed a cloud deal with Microsoft, with details to be shared next year. Cerebras now expects 2026 adjusted revenue of $940 million to $960 million, up from its previous expectations of $880 million to $890 million. Its adjusted cloud and services revenue, which reflects the OpenAI deal, more than tripled to $144.9 million for the third quarter. The chip firm posted an adjusted profit of $29.82 million in the third quarter, compared with an adjusted loss of $10.86 million a year earlier. Analysts, on average, had expected an adjusted loss of $38.4 million, according to data compiled by LSEG. Third-quarter adjusted sales rose 70 per cent to $230.9 million, beating analysts' average estimate of $214.70 million. In July, Cerebras announced a partnership with AMD to combine AMD's Helios systems with its wafer-scale engine for inference. Feldman said its cloud now uses AMD graphics processors for prompt processing. Cerebras' dinner-plate-sized WSE packs trillions of transistors on a single semiconductor and keeps memory on-chip, which it says is more efficient than linking many smaller GPUs that rely on costly high-bandwidth memory. Last month, Oracle expanded its cloud AI chip deals to add offerings from Cerebras. Feldman said the hardware will run in Oracle data centers, with the inference service expected to launch in summer 2027. He also said OpenAI's business with Cerebras grew from the second quarter, but that Cerebras lacked the capacity to support a broad rollout of OpenAI's Ultrafast, a faster service tier the AI firm previewed in August for its GPT-5.6 Sol model. He said data center availability remains a constraint across the industry and that US policy changes could create greater challenges for development.

Nov 12 : By one of Wall Street’s favorite metrics, Nvidia shares look like a bargain. Following a steep drop from its October 6 record high, Nvidia’s stock is trading at the equivalent of 12 times expected earnings. That’s its lowest valuation since 2012, when the chipmaker was competing with Advanced Micro Devices to dominate the market for videogame graphics cards while struggling to find a foothold in tablets and other mobile devices. The stock was down more than 5 per cent on Thursday after CEO Jensen Huang resigned, and is down about 12 per cent this week amid a scandal over reports of his extramarital affairs, including one with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress is taking over as interim CEO as Nvidia looks for a permanent successor.

But concern about leadership is not the only thing that has troubled investors. Nvidia, whose GPUs have fueled the AI boom, is now down over 30 per cent from its record, in large part due to worries about a potential slowdown in the buildout of AI data centers. "This is a key-person event, not a demand event. Nobody is canceling GPU orders because the CEO resigned. Historically, stocks take time to find a bottom after an abrupt CEO exit while the market works through the investigations and the search," said Erik Kratz, co-head of wealth and chief investment officer at Arena Private Wealth in Chicago. Nvidia reports quarterly earnings on Tuesday, with investors watching whether its sharp growth can survive without Huang. Investors favor stocks with low price-to-earnings ratios, or PEs, but a low multiple can also reflect doubts that expected earnings will materialize. While Nvidia’s share price has slumped in recent weeks, analysts so far have maintained forecasts for strong profit growth, expecting demand for Nvidia’s chips to continue to outpace supply. That could change after Nvidia posts its quarterly results. Analysts on average expect Nvidia to report a 92 per cent surge in October-quarter revenue and a net profit of over $60 billion, an 89 per cent increase, year over year, according to LSEG data. Investors will be keen to hear what Kress says about Nvidia’s outlook, which may matter even more than the results themselves.

Nov 12 : As Jensen Huang used Nvidia's swelling cash pile to bankroll the AI boom, his involvement went far beyond writing checks.     The Nvidia CEO dug deep into startups' technology, helped them secure customers within his company and even joined fundraising calls to attract investors, according to startup founders, venture capitalists and a former Nvidia employee. "We don't pick winners. We need to support everyone," Huang said on an episode of the "Dwarkesh" podcast in April.  The 63-year-old brought the same intensity to running his roughly $4 trillion chip giant, overseeing some 60 direct reports and personally diving into problems across the company.

That hands-on approach helped make him one of the AI industry's most powerful figures, with influence stretching from Silicon Valley to Washington, where he forged close ties with President Donald Trump and helped shape US chip export policy. It also made him one of the AI boom's great financiers with investments spanning AI cloud providers such as CoreWeave and Nebius and suppliers to the biggest labs. Until it all unraveled on Thursday. First, reports emerged that Huang had an affair with a Chinese businesswoman whom US authorities identified as a spy for Beijing. Nvidia's board launched an investigation and Huang apologized for his actions: "There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry." The crisis deepened on Wednesday after the New York Times reported Huang had a second affair, this time with an employee who directly reported to him. The board met later in the day and about 42 minutes before market open on Thursday, Nvidia announced Huang was out as CEO. The exit now raises questions about whether Nvidia and the AI ecosystem he helped build can thrive without him. "The bigger concern for me is not the next few quarters but the next decade," said Dan Sheehan, director of portfolio management at Telos Wealth Advisors.  "To find someone who can not only manage an extraordinary business but also continue to innovate and anticipate where the industry is heading. That's a very different challenge."  For now, Nvidia has named Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress interim CEO as it searches for a permanent successor, considering both internal and external candidates. Along with Kress, Ian Buck, who manages hardware and software products as head of product for hyperscale AI, as well as Arm chief Rene Haas, are seen as potential candidates.  Analysts say any successor will have to combine the technical expertise required to run a cutting-edge chipmaker with deep ties across the industry as well as in Washington, where Democrats now control both houses of Congress following a midterm sweep that included campaigns against data centers. "In truth, (it) will be very challenging to find a single person to replace him, so while I expect only one CEO, we could see several high-level hires or promotions that take on different aspects of what Jensen did," said Bob O'Donnell, President and Chief Analyst, TECHnalysis Research. Beyond the operational roles, analysts agree there is one aspect that will be much harder to replace - the cultural clout that made Huang the face of the AI boom, with so much influence that his mere mention of a company could move its shares. "Nvidia has lost the man who helped create the AI revolution, but it hasn't lost the technology driving it," said Sheehan. "The next CEO inherits an extraordinary business, but also one of the hardest acts to follow in corporate history."

Source: Reuters

NEW YORK, Nov 12 : Retail bought the Nvidia dip on Thursday in a big way, showing the AI trade is very much alive despite CEO Jensen Huang’s departure. Nvidia was off 5 per cent on Thursday afternoon following Huang’s resignation, which followed a report on Wednesday that the founder of the second most-valuable US-listed firm had an affair with a company executive who reported to him.  Thursday’s drop put Nvidia’s market-value decline for the week at $550 billion, with selling driven initially by questions about Huang’s relationship with a woman alleged to be a spy for Beijing. But buying the dip has been favored by investors ever since the end of the financial crisis in 2009, and Thursday was no different.  “Every time it works, it gets further reinforced,” said Mark Hackett, chief market strategist at Nationwide Financial in Downingtown, Pennsylvania. “It’s the kind of idiosyncratic behavior that you get in a healthy market.”

The rebound came after Nvidia tumbled as much as 14 per cent at Thursday’s open, extending a torrent of selling over the past month. Vanda Research called Thursday's open the biggest-ever first-half-hour retail flow into Nvidia, estimated at $111 million.   "I said to somebody an hour ago in the office, this feels like the calmest day in markets in a few weeks, which is insane given the news since the last close,” said Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager at Argent Capital Management in St. Louis, Missouri. “I think that a lot of damage has been done to Nvidia stock over the last couple of weeks.”  Nvidia stock has lost nearly a third of its value in the five weeks since the Nasdaq Composite hit its most recent high, shedding more than $1 trillion in market value.  On Thursday, retail buyers flocked to popular investment platforms. At Fidelity Investments, customers had placed 394,818 buy orders for Nvidia by noon ET, compared with 80,088 sell orders. Buy orders for Nvidia more than doubled the combined buy orders on Thursday for the nine other most-traded stocks on the platform, with runner-up Advanced Micro Devices showing 24,790 buy orders and third-placed Nebius amassing 24,519. Sentiment was hardly unanimous. On Reddit's popular wallstreetbets trading forum, 60 per cent of comments about Nvidia were negative. A wave of Wall Street downgrades this week hasn’t helped, with analysts at Baird Equity Research on Wednesday cutting the stock to neutral and slashing their price target by 60 per cent to $200 a share, which is still far above Thursday’s afternoon price of $164. “2027 data center forecasts are being delayed due to very recent lack of visibility, with supply issues mostly the reason for a potential slowdown but also due to potential demand softening. AI hyperscaler capex could slow to 40 per cent growth or slightly less for 2027,” senior research analyst Tristan Gerra wrote.  Looking ahead, investors said the key issues for the market include what Nvidia executives say on next Tuesday’s quarterly earnings conference call and Anthropic’s IPO, which is expected to come to market later next week.  “The outlook for AI is going to be just fine,” said Hackett. He said he believes the Anthropic IPO is likely the more important event next week because, with Nvidia’s new management just having started, “It’s going to be hard for them to get a get out of jail free card out of one conference call.”

NEW YORK, Nov 12 : Options traders cashed in parts of their bets against Nvidia and positioned for a longer-term share price recovery on Thursday, after CEO Jensen Huang announced he was stepping down. Huang's departure has raised uncertainty over the future direction of the AI chipmaker he built into one of the world's most valuable companies. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO as the company searches for a permanent successor. The leadership turmoil sent options volatility soaring on Thursday, but options trading suggested that investors were repositioning for a recovery rather than fleeing the stock.  "Nvida's competitive advantage and customers don't disappear overnight," said Seth Hickle, chief investment officer at Mindset Wealth Management. "The market is trying to determine whether this is a temporary leadership crisis or something that fundamentally changes the AI investment thesis."

Options give holders the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell the underlying stock at a set price before a certain date. Call options typically gain value when the stock rises, while puts gain when it falls. Several large options trades showed investors rolling bullish positions further into 2027, lowering upside targets and taking profits on downside hedges rather than abandoning exposure to the company altogether, data from Chris Murphy, co-head of derivatives strategy at Susquehanna, showed. In one trade, an investor sold put options and bought cheaper ones, collecting about $18.9 million while keeping some protection against a further drop, Murphy said. Another investor paid about $18.8 million for call spreads, a bet that pays off fully if Nvidia climbs about 16 per cent from current levels by March. Other trades pushed bullish positions out by three months and lowered the price targets, adding time for a recovery to play out. Investors also bought about 50,000 January call options, spending an estimated $45.3 million to $55 million to bet the shares will rise above current levels by expiry. Nvidia's shares were last down 4.84 per cent at $165.40. Nvidia's 90-day implied volatility has climbed to about 52 per cent from roughly 33 per cent a month ago, reflecting growing uncertainty ahead of the company's earnings report next week, according to Susquehanna data. "Implied (volatility) will remain high until the earnings report, and subsequently the conference call as it can shed some clarity about how Nvidia plans to move forward past this boondoggle," Hickle said.

NEW YORK, Nov 12 : Kalshi has ended its advisory contract with Donald Trump Jr after his venture capital firm 1789 Capital increased its stake in arch-rival Polymarket, according to a spokesperson for the $40 billion prediction markets startup. The Democratic sweep of both houses of US Congress in the midterm elections could bring more scrutiny of companies over links to the White House. Democrats have said they plan to use investigative powers on President Donald Trump's family business ties. Kalshi had named Trump Jr a "strategic advisor" in January 2025. Trump Jr was given a stake in the company that the Financial Times reported at the time was worth $300,000. "We have mutually agreed to end Don's advisory role after his firm's significant investment in a competitor this past summer. We are grateful for his contributions in helping us market Kalshi to more customers," the spokesperson said, adding that the conversations to end the contract started in August since 1789 led Polymarket's most recent funding round.

The Kalshi spokesperson said that there were no political considerations that factored into the decision. Two sources familiar with the matter said there had been some concerns raised within the company about potential ramifications of the Democratic sweep. Specifically, the sources said that having the president's son as an adviser might open the company up to scrutiny by the US Congress. The Kalshi spokesperson said the company had not considered or discussed political implications. Kalshi sought inroads with various demographic and political groups in early 2025, according to a third source familiar with the matter. That source said Kalshi contracted with Donald Trump Jr at the time, paying him in equity for guidance in marketing itself to a conservative audience including the MAGA movement. A Polymarket spokesperson declined to comment. Donald Trump Jr did not immediately respond to a request for comment. A representative for 1789 Capital declined to comment. Kalshi started discussing 1789's most recent investment in Polymarket in August when news of the venture capital firm's bet became public, according to a person familiar with the matter. Kalshi reached out to Trump Jr during the fall to discuss the conflict of interest, the source added. GREATER SCRUTINY Prediction markets first rose to prominence in 2024 as they strongly diverged from traditional opinion polls by signaling a Trump victory. Kalshi, at the time, boasted about the accuracy of its own forecasts, while criticizing pollsters and "traditional media" for failing to anticipate Trump’s "decisive victory." Campaign finance and other records show both firms this year have made substantial political donations to both parties, Reuters has reported. Now, such platforms face the prospect of heightened scrutiny in the US Congress. Senator Elizabeth Warren, for instance, has vowed to crack down on insider trading on prediction markets. Earlier this year, Senator Chris Murphy and Representative Greg Casar, both Democrats, introduced a bill to ban prediction market bets on military operations and other sensitive government actions. Several other efforts to rein in prediction markets are also moving forward on Capitol Hill, after a series of well-timed market bets this year fueled questions about insider trading on these platforms, while stoking concerns over the legality and ethics of such trades.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns amid deepening scandal, leaving AI chip giant at crossroads

Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will take over as interim CEO. Jensen Huang, who co-founded Nvidia, will not remain on the board.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang stepped down on Thursday (Nov 12) after revelations of two extramarital affairs , including one involving a suspected Chinese spy , plunged the chipmaker into crisis and sent shockwaves across an AI industry he helped bankroll. Huang's exit caps a tumultuous week for Nvidia , one of the major engines behind the AI boom, and could have far-reaching consequences for US chip export policy and the broader AI ecosystem, given the ex-CEO's push to preserve access to the Chinese market, as well as his close ties with US President Donald Trump. The crisis has threatened to implicate some Trump administration members, including Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who is facing growing questions over the administration's oversight of chip sales to China, particularly as both he and Huang pushed for relaxing those sales despite scrutiny from longtime China hawks in both parties. The Commerce Department did not immediately comment. Senior White House officials are discussing whether Lutnick should be pushed out, two people familiar with the situation told Reuters on Thursday.

The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Lutnick's future. Earlier in the day, a White House official said US President Donald Trump "maintains complete confidence in the secretary and his ability to carry out the position." Huang's departure threatens to disrupt an AI ecosystem that he helped shape by pouring Nvidia 's swelling cash pile back into cloud providers, suppliers and the industry's biggest labs. The surge in AI computing demand drove a sevenfold increase in Nvidia 's shares through early October, pushing its market value at one point to nearly US$6 trillion. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will take over as interim CEO as Nvidia looks for a permanent successor, considering both internal and external candidates, the company said on Thursday.

Related:

Who would be next CEO at Nvidia? Top engineer and CFO favoured as candidates

Jensen Huang scandal could spur tighter US scrutiny of AI cloud providers in Southeast Asia: Analysts

The departure has also ignited speculation over who will ultimately lead the company, long associated with the leather-jacket-wearing Huang, who co-founded Nvidia more than three decades ago. Kress and longtime Nvidia engineer Ian Buck had emerged as the leading internal candidates among investors and analysts even before Huang's departure. Nvidia shares were down about 4.8 per cent, paring earlier losses. Shares of rivals AMD and Broadcom rose about 6 per cent each. Huang, Nvidia 's fourth-largest shareholder with a 3.61 per cent stake, will also leave the board. Nvidia named former Synopsys CEO and longtime director Harvey Jones as its first board chair. "The Board, Estaff (executive staff) and I recognize that this has been an extraordinarily difficult period," Kress wrote in a memo to employees, adding that the company will host a meeting on Nov 18. Kress was gathering Nvidia 's executive team at its headquarters on Thursday, CNBC reported, adding that Huang had agreed to testify before Congress before Thanksgiving. Huang has hired law firm Paul Weiss, the New York Times reported, citing two people familiar with the matter. It was not clear what the firm had been retained to do, the report said. The company has not commented beyond its statement announcing Huang's resignation. REPLACING HUANG Pressure had been mounting on Huang in recent days after reports said the 63-year-old, who is married, had an affair with a Chinese businesswoman whom US authorities suspect of spying for Beijing. The New York Times also reported Wednesday that Huang had an extramarital affair with a senior company executive who reported to him. While Kress offers investors a familiar hand after 13 years as CFO, analysts have pointed to Buck as a potential longer-term candidate because of Nvidia 's reliance on technical leadership. The veteran engineer helped develop its crucial CUDA software platform and now leads its hyperscale AI products. "The risk is not that Nvidia suddenly loses its technology roadmap ... that roadmap is largely visible for the next several years. The risk is execution. Jensen has been the chief conductor of an extraordinarily complex system," said Michael Feldman, portfolio manager at ClearBridge Investments. "In a world with real bottlenecks, that coordination is a competitive advantage in itself." Investor sentiment toward AI stocks has already been shaky as soaring cash burn and rising debt at traditionally cash-rich tech giants fuel doubts over whether the AI boom will pay off.

TRUMP WEIGHS IN Trump said on Sunday that Huang had "done an amazing job for our country" and that the Nvidia chief had told him he had no idea the Chinese woman he had an affair with was a spy. Trump had urged Huang to fight for his job in a call on Tuesday, the New York Times reported. On Thursday, the US president suggested former Apple CEO Tim Cook should take over as Nvidia 's CEO. US House Speaker Mike Johnson said it was "critically important for right successor to be chosen to replace Huang", noting there was a growing consensus in Congress on limiting exports of semiconductor chips to China. HUANG'S ROCK-STAR STATUS For years, Nvidia was best known to gamers chasing top-tier graphics. But its chips' ability to perform many calculations at once has made them the oil of the AI boom and a strategic prize in the US-China race to dominate the technology. It also made Nvidia the world's most valuable company. That turned Huang into a rock-star CEO, mobbed by fans in Taiwan and South Korea who ask him to sign books, posters and sometimes even their bodies. The scandal preceding Huang's departure unfolded over more than a year, beginning with an October 2025 New York Times report linking him to Alice Huang , a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, a coveted official Nvidia cloud partner with priority access to its chips. Subsequent reports said US intelligence officials believed Alice Huang was acting on behalf of Chinese intelligence. Beijing has denied Alice Huang is a spy. Washington has also investigated Megaspeed over suspicions it helped China obtain advanced AI chips restricted under US export controls, according to media reports.

Related:

Alice Huang barred from re-entering Singapore; insufficient evidence she committed offences in Megaspeed probe: MHA

What we know about Megaspeed, Singapore-based customer of Nvidia

Separately, Bloomberg News reported on Thursday that the US Justice Department was investigating Alice Huang over whether entities linked to her were involved in efforts to smuggle Super Micro Computer products to China, citing a person familiar with the matter. A spokesperson for the Manhattan US Attorney’s office declined to comment on the Bloomberg report. The office previously charged three people associated with Super Micro, including its co-founder, with helping smuggle at least US$2.5 billion of US AI technology to China in violation of export laws. Super Micro did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. Earlier, the Singapore Ministry of Home Affairs said Singapore police had been investigating Super Micro as part of a wider probe into Megaspeed and Alice Huang. The police had reached out to the FBI and the Justice Department for help and had received "limited information or assistance," the ministry said. Earlier this month, Nvidia 's board launched a probe, led by independent directors with outside legal counsel, into whether Jensen Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. It also expressed confidence in him at the time. The controversy escalated on Wednesday when the New York Times reported Huang also had an affair with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia 's vice president of healthcare, who reported to him.
